parameters.content:
## One blog post -> a LinkedIn video, an X teaser and an OG image

Every morning this workflow reads your blog feed, and when there is a new post it
makes **one** LLM call to write the social copy, then renders **three assets that
share one brand system**:

| Piece | Size | Format |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LinkedIn square video | 1080x1080 | mp4, ~20 s |
| X teaser video | 1280x720 | mp4, ~8 s |
| Open Graph share image | 1200x630 | png |

### Setup (about four minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **OpenRouter** — add an **OpenRouter** credential and attach it to
   *Write kit copy*. Any JSON-capable model works; `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` is the
   default because it is cheap and obeys word budgets.
3. **Open `Config`** — set `feedUrl` to your blog's RSS URL, then `brandName`,
   `domainOverride` and the two brand colours.
4. **Run it — the first run renders for real and spends 29 credits at the
   defaults** (20 + 8 + 1 for the three pieces). `dryRun` is `false` out of the
   box. When it finishes, click **▶ Watch video**: n8n plays both videos and
   shows the image inline, one output item per piece.
5. Want a free preview first? Set `dryRun: true` in **Config**: you get the
   credit quote per piece plus an **editorLink** for each, nothing spent.
6. **Activate** — it builds a kit for every new post, once a day at 9am.

## The feed is the trigger

*Read blog feed* is the stock **RSS Feed Read** node — it works untouched on
n8n Cloud, no community node required.

*Pick newest post* takes the newest feed entry. *Run summary* then writes that
post's `guid` into workflow static data — but **only once all three pieces have
finished rendering**, so a half-failed run is retried in full instead of being
silently skipped. An activated workflow therefore makes exactly one kit per
published post and quietly reports "nothing new" the rest of the time.

**Static data only persists on production executions**, so while the workflow is
inactive your manual test runs never advance the marker — handy while you are
setting the brand up, and the reason repeated manual runs re-render the same post.

*Fetch post page* is best-effort: it pulls the article body when the feed only
carries a one-line snippet, and simply continues when the page blocks it.

## One LLM call, six strings, hard clamps

*Write kit copy* asks for exactly six things — `liHeadline`, three `liPoints`,
`teaserHook`, `teaserLine`, `ogTitle` and `ogKicker` — each with a word budget
that matches the layout it lands in.

Models overshoot budgets. *Build project JSON* therefore **clamps every string
again**, by words first and then by characters, and appends an ellipsis when it
has to cut. Nothing the model returns can overflow a layout.

Every string is also HTML-escaped before it reaches the layout, so a post title
containing `&`, `<` or a quote renders as text rather than breaking the card.

Type scales with content too: the LinkedIn headline steps 104 -> 64 px as it
grows, the OG title 82 -> 52 px, and the brand+domain footer shrinks to stay
inside its column.

## Free preview: the optional dry run

**`dryRun` is `false` in Config, so a run renders all three pieces for real.**
Set it to `true` whenever you want a free pass instead: the workflow validates
each payload, quotes the exact credit cost per piece plus `kitCreditsTotal`, and
saves each one as a **draft**, reporting an **editorLink** like
`https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open them to see the exact assets and tweak anything by hand, with nothing spent.

Set `dryRun` back to `false` to render the kit.

## Three renders, one poll loop

The kit is three separate render jobs. *Submit render* runs once per piece,
*Attach job to piece* glues each `jobId` back onto its item, and the
Wait -> Get status -> Merge -> IF loop polls them together.

Pieces finish at different times: the image is nearly instant, the 8 s teaser is
quick, the 20 s LinkedIn video takes longest. Finished pieces leave the loop
immediately and flow to *Run summary*, so **that node can run more than once in
one execution** — each batch still reports the whole kit's `kitCreditsTotal`.

A failed render stops the run with the piece's name in the message. Nothing is
written anywhere else, so a re-run simply rebuilds the kit.

## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run. It downloads each finished asset as binary, and
n8n renders it inline by mime type — the two MP4s become video players, and the
OG image shows as a picture. One output item per kit piece, each with a download
button.

*Run summary* before it carries `videoUrl`, `kind`, `dimensions`,
`creditsCharged` and `kitCreditsTotal` if you want to pipe the results onward.

## Publishing the kit (optional tail)

The run ends with three URLs in *Run summary* — a clean handoff you can extend:

- **LinkedIn** — the square video is already the native LinkedIn format. Post it
  with a scheduler that accepts a public video URL (Blotato, Buffer, Metricool),
  or hand it to a human with a Slack/Email node.
- **X** — the 1280x720 teaser is standard h.264 landscape; the same schedulers
  take it directly.
- **The OG image** — upload it to your CMS or drop the URL straight into the
  post's meta tags:
  `<meta property="og:image" content="...">` and
  `<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">`.

Filter *Run summary* by `kind` (`linkedin-video`, `x-teaser-video`,
`og-image`) to route each piece to its own destination. These are left out of
the required path on purpose so the import runs with a Zvid key and an
OpenRouter key, nothing else.
